Split SWARM Clusters

Source: R/cluster_fun.R
split_swarm_clusters.Rd

During SWARM denoising (including when fastidious = TRUE and d = 1), ASVs differing by a single nucleotide can be grouped into the same cluster, even when they have comparable abundances. This function refines such clusters by identifying ASVs whose read counts exceed both a minimum relative abundance threshold (min_abundance_ratio) and a minimum absolute read count (min_read_count).

Usage

split_swarm_clusters(
  read_count,
  cluster,
  min_abundance_ratio = 0.1,
  min_read_count = 10,
  outfile = "",
  sep = ",",
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

read_count

Data frame or CSV file with the following variables: asv, sample, replicate (optional), read_count.

cluster

Data frame or CSV file with the following variables: asv_id, cluster_id.

min_abundance_ratio

Numeric; minimum ratio of an ASV's read count relative to the cluster centroid required for the ASV to define a new cluster (e.g., 0.2 corresponds to 20% of centroid abundance).

min_read_count

Numeric; minimum absolute read count required for an ASV to be considered for splitting.

outfile

Character string: name of the output CSV file. If empty, no file is written.

sep

Field separator character for input and output CSV files.

quiet

Logical; if TRUE, suppress informational messages and show only warnings or errors.

Value

A data frame with the same structure as the input. For each cluster–sample–replicate combination, ASVs are either:

  • split into multiple clusters defined by ASVs that meet the min_abundance_ratio and min_read_count criteria, with read counts redistributed while preserving relative abundances, or

  • pooled into a single row (reads summed across ASVs) if no ASV meets the splitting criteria.

Details

For each cluster, ASVs meeting both criteria are retained as independent units and each defines a new cluster. The total number of reads in the original cluster is then redistributed among these selected ASVs while preserving their relative abundances.

If no ASVs meet the criteria, reads are summed across ASVs within each cluster–sample–replicate combination, and the cluster is retained as a single unit.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
read_count_df <- split_swarm_clusters(
  read_count = read_count_df,
  min_abundance_ratio = 0.1,
  min_read_count = 10
)
} # }
